Matching the height lands the drawn width 0.94pp narrow; matching the width would leave the height 0.85pp tall and pull the crop off both anchored edges. A uniform scale cannot express a non-uniform stretch and the map should not try, so the height is the read and the 0.94pp is pinned by the test rather than left to drift. No browser ran. Both boards draw the fill at aspect 0.9672, wider than both cuts, so a cover fit matches HEIGHT and each h- is the zoom outright: 1.05860 here, 1.12930 there, and on BOTH boards the zoom read off the width equals the zoom read off the height to five decimals (gap 0.00000), so neither stretches its fill and both reproduce exactly under a uniform scale. Export the board's own ~0.9672 source and one per-width class (scale-[1.0586], lg:scale-[1.1293], origin-top) closes BOTH boards from ONE asset. Not built: new asset bytes are a design-pipeline act, and Figma's render is not the art pipeline's file. Casey call, now cheaper than the row carried. Also re-confirmed and not acted on: this board grounds on solid #3051AA where its neighbours ground on #001615, and its gradient start is 32.58% against the Desktop's 34.384% and the card's shared 41.8%. No browser ran, no asset touched.
